5 key factors that drive your cost
Complexity & features
More features = more hours. Real-time chat, payments, and dashboards cost significantly more than simple forms.
Technology stack
Laravel, React, and Next.js speed up development — meaning fewer billable hours and better long-term code.
Developer type
Freelancers charge $25–$80/hr. Agencies charge $80–$200/hr. Choosing right saves thousands.
Design complexity
Custom UI adds 15–50% to total cost. Templates are cheaper; bespoke animations cost the most.
Ongoing maintenance
Budget 15–20% of build cost annually for hosting, security patches, and updates.

5 ways to reduce your development cost
Start with an MVP. Build only what you need to launch. Cut nice-to-have features for version 2. This alone can cut your initial budget by 40–60%.
Choose the right tech stack. Laravel + Next.js speed up development significantly, meaning fewer billable hours for the same quality output.
Use open-source tools. Auth, payments, and admin panels don't need to be built from scratch. Proven packages save dozens of billable hours.
Have a clear project scope. Changing requirements mid-project is the #1 cause of budget overruns. A clear brief = a more accurate quote.
Hire a skilled freelancer. A senior freelance developer often delivers better results than an agency for small-to-mid projects, at half the cost.
Frequently asked questions
QuestionAnswer
How long does it take?Simple apps: 4–8 weeks. Mid apps: 3–5 months. Enterprise: 6–18 months.
Can I build for under $5,000?Yes, for a simple website. For user accounts or payments, budget at least $8,000–$15,000.
Is Laravel good in 2025?Absolutely — it's the most popular PHP framework, used by millions of apps worldwide.
Is Next.js better than WordPress?For performance and SEO, yes. Faster loads, better Core Web Vitals, and more flexibility.
How much is annual maintenance?Budget 15–20% of the original build cost per year for updates, hosting, and security.
